stem: Consider the following statements: (1) The external forces are known as exogenic forces. (2) The internal forces are known as endogenic forces. (3) Wearing down relief variations of the surface of the earth through erosion is known as gradation. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: External forces are exogenic and internal forces are endogenic, so (1) and (2) are correct. Gradation is the levelling of relief variations of the surface through erosion and deposition, so (3) is also correct. All three are correct. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) The exogenic and endogenic forces give rise to the geomorphic processes. (2) Diastrophism and volcanism are exogenic geomorphic processes. (3) Mass wasting, erosion and deposition are exogenic geomorphic processes. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Statement (1) is correct. Diastrophism and volcanism are endogenic (internal) processes, not exogenic, so (2) is wrong. Mass wasting, erosion and deposition are exogenic, so (3) is correct. Correct statements are (1) and (3). Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not an exogenic process?
solution: Weathering, mass wasting and deposition are exogenic (external) processes. Diastrophism is an endogenic (internal) process. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Gravitational stresses are as important as the other geomorphic processes. (2) The movements of materials either within the earth or on the surface of the earth occur due to pressure gradient. Which of the above is incorrect?
solution: Gravitational stresses are indeed as important as other geomorphic processes, so (1) is correct. All movements occur due to gradients, including pressure gradients, so (2) is correct. Neither statement is incorrect. Matches option D.

subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following is the driving force for endogenic geomorphic processes?
optA: Radioactive nature of the particles present in the earth's interior
optB: Rotational forces generated by the earth's rotation
optC: Both of the a and b
optD: None of the a and b
solution: The energy for endogenic processes comes from within the earth, generated mainly by radioactivity, rotational and tidal friction, and primordial heat. Both the radioactivity of the interior and rotational forces contribute. Matches option C.

subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Consider the following statements about diastrophism: (1) These processes elevate or build up portions of the earth's crust. (2) Orogenic processes help in coast building. (3) Epeirogenic processes involve uplift or warping of large parts of the earth's crust. (4) Plate tectonics involves vertical movements of crustal plates. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Diastrophism elevates or builds up parts of the crust, so (1) is correct. Orogeny is mountain building, not coast building, so (2) is wrong. Epeirogeny is continental building involving uplift or warping, so (3) is correct. Plate tectonics involves horizontal (not vertical) movements of plates, so (4) is wrong. Correct statements are (1) and (3). Matches option A.

subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Which of the following helps in the continental building?
solution: Epeirogeny is the continental building process, involving broad uplift or warping of large parts of the crust. Orogeny is mountain building. Matches option B.

subtopic: Earth's Interior, Crust and Plate Tectonics
stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Diastrophism processes also cause metamorphism of rocks. (2) Orogeny is a mountain building process whereas epeirogeny is a continental building process. Which of the above is/are not correct?
solution: Diastrophism (through heat and pressure) does cause metamorphism of rocks, so (1) is correct. Orogeny is mountain building and epeirogeny is continental building, so (2) is correct. Neither is incorrect. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements about the exogenic processes: (1) Temperature and precipitation are the two important climatic elements that control various exogenic processes. (2) Weathering, mass wasting/movements, erosion and transportation are included in denudation. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Temperature and precipitation are the two key climatic elements controlling exogenic processes, so (1) is correct. Denudation includes weathering, mass wasting/movements, erosion and transportation, so (2) is correct. Both are correct. Matches option A.

stem: Which of the following will not cause the weathering of rocks?
solution: Weathering is caused by chemical, physical/mechanical and biological agents. Volcanic eruption is an endogenic process, not a weathering agent. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following: (1) Electromagnetic radiation. (2) Geothermal energy. (3) Gravitational force. (4) Plate movements. (5) Rotation of the Earth. (6) Revolution of the Earth. Which of the above are responsible for bringing dynamic changes on the surface of Earth?
solution: Solar (electromagnetic) radiation drives exogenic processes; geothermal energy and plate movements drive endogenic processes; gravitational force drives all downslope movements; and the earth's rotation and revolution influence winds, currents and seasonal changes. All of these bring dynamic changes to the surface. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Derived; the intended key is 'All of these' as every listed factor contributes to the earth's surface dynamism. Verify against the source's intended key.

stem: The process by which rock particles are reduced in size by rubbing against each other or against the surface during transport by wind, water or ice is referred to as
solution: Reduction of particle size by mutual rubbing during transport is attrition (a form of abrasion). Deflation is the removal of loose material by wind, exfoliation is the peeling of rock sheets, and solution is dissolving of minerals. None of the given options names this process. Matches option D.
reviewNote: DISAGREES with official key (B, Exfoliation). Exfoliation is the peeling of rock sheets by pressure release/temperature, NOT particle reduction by rubbing during transport (attrition); so the described process matches none of the options -> D. The official key B appears factually incorrect.

stem: Which of the following is not correct about chemical weathering?
optA: Solution, carbonation, hydration, oxidation and reduction are some of the processes included in chemical weathering.
optB: Water and air (oxygen and carbon dioxide) along with heat must be present to speed up all chemical reactions.
optC: Decomposition of plants and animals decreases the quantity of carbon dioxide underground.
solution: Solution, carbonation, hydration, oxidation and reduction are chemical weathering processes, so (A) is correct. Water, air and heat speed up chemical reactions, so (B) is correct. Decomposition of plants and animals releases carbon dioxide, so it increases (not decreases) the carbon dioxide underground; (C) is therefore incorrect. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the below are causing factors of physical weathering? (1) Gravitational forces. (2) Temperature. (3) Alternate dry and wet climate. (4) Magma movement.
solution: Physical (mechanical) weathering is driven by gravitational (unloading/pressure-release) forces, temperature changes, and alternate wetting and drying. Magma movement is an endogenic process, not a weathering agent. Correct factors are (1), (2) and (3). Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following is not true about biological weathering?
optA: Burrowing and wedging by organisms like earthworms, termites, rodents etc.
optC: Ploughing and cultivating soils for agriculture.
solution: Biological weathering includes burrowing and wedging by organisms and human disturbance such as ploughing and cultivating soils. Mass movement is a separate gravity-driven transport process, not a form of weathering. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Derived; 'Mass movements' is the clearest non-weathering item. 'Deep drilling by humans' (B) is also arguably not biological weathering — confirm the intended key.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Exfoliation can occur due to expansion and contraction induced by temperature changes. (2) Weathering process helps in the formation of the soil. (3) Weathering of rocks and deposits helps in the enrichment and concentrations of certain valuable ores of iron, manganese, aluminium, copper etc. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Exfoliation results from expansion and contraction due to temperature changes, so (1) is correct. Weathering is essential for soil formation, so (2) is correct. Weathering enriches and concentrates ores such as iron, manganese, aluminium and copper, so (3) is correct. All three are correct. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Mass movements are not very active over weathered slopes rather than over unweathered materials. (2) Gravitational gradient plays an important role in the process of mass movement. (3) Abundant precipitation and torrential rains and scarcity of vegetation etc. favour mass movements. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: Mass movements are actually MORE active over weathered slopes than over unweathered materials, so (1) is wrong. Gravity (gravitational gradient) is the driving force of mass movement, so (2) is correct. Abundant precipitation, torrential rains and scarcity of vegetation favour mass movements, so (3) is correct. Correct statements are (2) and (3). Matches option B.

stem: Which of the below is not correct?
optA: Landslides are relatively rapid and perceptible movements.
optB: Deforestation does not lead to landslides.
optC: Landslides are common in mountain regions.
optD: Heavy raining and cloud bursts also can cause landslides.
solution: Landslides are rapid, perceptible mass movements common in mountain regions and triggered by heavy rain and cloud bursts, so (A), (C) and (D) are correct. Deforestation removes the binding effect of roots and does lead to landslides, so (B) is incorrect. Matches option B.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Mechanical weathering due to temperature changes and ranges is pronounced in the western ghats region. (2) Debris avalanches and landslides occur very frequently in the Himalayan region. (3) Himalayan region is made up of hard and stable rocks. How many of the above is/are correct?
solution: The Western Ghats are humid, where chemical (not mechanical) weathering dominates, so (1) is wrong. Debris avalanches and landslides are very frequent in the Himalayas, so (2) is correct. The Himalayas are young fold mountains made of weak, unstable rocks, not hard and stable ones, so (3) is wrong. Only one statement is correct. Matches option A.
reviewNote: DISAGREES with official key (B, meaning 2 statements correct). Only statement (2) is true; statement (1) is false (thermal/mechanical weathering is a desert phenomenon, not the humid Western Ghats) and statement (3) is false (Himalayas are young, weak, unstable rocks). So exactly one is correct -> A. The official key B appears incorrect (it likely counts the false Western-Ghats statement as true).

stem: Which of the following influences the formation of deltas? (1) Tides (2) Currents (3) Waves (4) Rate of sedimentation. Select the correct answer from the following codes:
solution: A delta forms where a river's rate of sedimentation exceeds the removal of sediment by tides, currents and waves. All four factors — tides, currents, waves and the rate of sedimentation — influence delta formation. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) The main work of the river is deposition and erosion. (2) Deltas do not obstruct the river flow. Select the correct answer from the following codes:
solution: A river's main work is erosion, transportation and deposition, so (1) is acceptable. Deltas split the river into distributaries and do obstruct/divide the flow, so (2) is wrong. Only (1) is correct. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Estuaries are more suitable for large ports than deltas. (2) Rivers are used to export bulky goods, import food stuffs, and raw materials. Select the correct answer from the following codes:
solution: Estuaries offer deep water and are more suitable for large ports than shallow, sediment-choked deltas, so (1) is correct. Rivers and inland waterways are used to move bulky goods, food stuffs and raw materials, so (2) is correct. Both are correct. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is formed in the youthful stage of the river? (1) V shaped valley (2) Waterfalls (3) Rapids (4) Meanders
solution: In the youthful stage the river cuts down vigorously, producing V-shaped valleys, waterfalls and rapids. Meanders develop in the mature stage, not the youthful stage. Correct features are (1), (2) and (3). Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following: (1) Potholes, plunge pools and valleys are depositional landforms of the river. (2) River terraces and braided channels are erosional landforms of the river. Which of the above is correct?
solution: Potholes, plunge pools and valleys are erosional (not depositional) landforms, so (1) is wrong. Braided channels are depositional landforms, so calling them erosional in (2) is wrong. Neither statement is correct. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Alluvial fans are formed when streams flowing from higher levels break into foot slope plains of low gradient. (2) Deltas are like alluvial fans but develop at the mouth of the river. (3) Floodplains, Natural Levees and Point Bars are depositional landforms. (4) Meanders are formed in the youthful stage of the river. How many of the above are not correct?
solution: Statements (1), (2) and (3) are all correct descriptions of fluvial depositional landforms. Meanders form in the mature stage, not the youthful stage, so (4) is not correct. Exactly one statement is not correct. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following: (1) Moraines and eskers are depositional features of glaciers. (2) Cirque and horns are erosional features of glaciers. Which of the above is incorrect?
solution: Moraines and eskers are glacial depositional features, so (1) is correct. Cirques and horns are glacial erosional features, so (2) is correct. Neither statement is incorrect. Matches option D.

stem: Very deep glacial troughs filled with sea water and making up shorelines (in high latitudes) are called:
solution: Deep glacial troughs drowned by sea water along high-latitude coasts are fiords (fjords). Aretes are sharp glacial ridges, moraines are glacial deposits, and 'stalks' is not a glacial landform. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following: (1) Stalagmites rise up from the floor of the caves. (2) Pillars are formed by the erosional effect of groundwater on the adjacent rocks. (3) Stalactites hang as icicles of different diameters. How many of the above are correct?
solution: Stalagmites rise from the cave floor, so (1) is correct. Pillars form by the depositional joining of a stalactite and a stalagmite, not by erosion, so (2) is wrong. Stalactites hang from the roof like icicles of varying diameters, so (3) is correct. Two statements are correct. Matches option B.

stem: Doline is formed by the:
solution: A doline (sinkhole) is a solution hollow produced by the erosional (solution) action of groundwater on limestone. Matches option D.

stem: Karst landforms are made by:
solution: Karst landforms develop through the solution and deposition action of water in limestone (soluble rock) regions. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is not an erosional landform made by the groundwater?
solution: Lapies, limestone pavements and uvalas are erosional (solution) landforms of groundwater. Stalactites are depositional landforms formed by the deposition of calcium carbonate. Matches option D.

stem: Which one of the following is not a fluvial landform?
solution: Gorges, braids and canyons are all landforms made by running water (fluvial). A cirque is a glacial erosional landform. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Gently inclined rocky floors close to the mountains at their foot, with or without a thin cover of debris, are called pediments. (2) Inselberg, which is a remnant of the mountain, is formed due to wind erosion. (3) The playa plain covered up by salts is called alkali flats. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
solution: Gently inclined rocky floors at the mountain foot are pediments, so (1) is correct. Per NCERT, inselbergs are residual hills produced by weathering and the erosional work of running water (sheet flooding) as pediments extend, not by wind erosion, so (2) is wrong. A salt-covered playa plain is called alkali flats, so (3) is correct. Correct statements are (1) and (3). Matches option C.
reviewNote: DISAGREES with official key (D, all correct). NCERT attributes inselberg/pediment evolution to running water + weathering, so statement (2) 'formed due to wind erosion' is imprecise/false -> C. The official D reflects the common exam simplification that all desert landforms are wind-made; DEBATABLE — keep C (NCERT-precise) or adopt D if grading strictly to the teacher's key.

stem: Consider the statements about the sand dunes: (1) Seif is similar to barchan with a small difference. Seif has two wings or points. (2) Crescent shaped dunes are called barchans. (3) Longitudinal dunes form when supply of sand is poor and wind direction is constant. (4) Transverse dunes are aligned perpendicular to wind direction. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: A seif is similar to a barchan but has only ONE wing or point (a barchan has two), so (1) is wrong. Crescent-shaped dunes are barchans, so (2) is correct. Longitudinal dunes form where sand supply is poor and wind direction is constant, so (3) is correct. Transverse dunes lie perpendicular to the wind direction, so (4) is correct. Correct statements are (2), (3) and (4). Matches option B.

stem: Which one of the following sentences best defines the term 'Lapies'?
optA: A small to medium sized shallow depression
optB: A landform whose opening is more or less circular at the top and funnel shaped towards bottom
optC: A landform formed due to dripping water from surface
optD: An irregular surface with sharp pinnacles, grooves and ridges
solution: Lapies is an irregular limestone surface with sharp pinnacles, grooves and ridges produced by solution along joints. The other options describe sinkholes/dolines and dripstone features. Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following distinct features are found on glacial topography? (a) drumlin (b) Yardang (c) hanging valley (d) sand beach
solution: Drumlins and hanging valleys are glacial landforms. Yardangs are wind-eroded landforms and sand beaches are coastal. So the glacial features are (a) and (c). Matches option C.

stem: Statement I: Incised meanders are formed in the mature stage of a river. Statement II: Incised meanders are characterised by rejuvenation and upliftment of land. Codes:
optA: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
optB: Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
optC: Statement I is true, but statement II is false
optD: Statement I is false, but statement II is true
solution: Meanders develop in the mature stage of a river; when the land is uplifted (rejuvenation), the river cuts vertically into these pre-existing meanders to form incised meanders. Both statements are true, and the rejuvenation and upliftment in Statement II correctly explain the formation of incised meanders in Statement I. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Derived assertion-reason; both statements true with II explaining I. Confirm the intended key.

stem: Which of these features is produced by wind erosion and deposition? (I) Seif (II) Spit (III) Barchan (IV) Zeugen. Codes:
solution: Seif and barchan are wind-deposited dunes, and zeugen is a wind-eroded landform, so all three are aeolian. A spit is a coastal depositional landform, not a wind feature. Correct features are (I), (III) and (IV). Matches option D.

stem: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
solution: Canyon is fluvial, zeugen is aeolian and moraine is glacial — all correctly matched. Inselberg is an arid/desert residual landform, not a glacial one, so 'Inselberg - glacier' is wrongly matched. Matches option C.

stem: Small lakes formed by glacial erosion are known as:
solution: Small lakes occupying glacially-eroded rock basins (such as cirques) are called tarns. Playas are desert lakes and roche moutonnee are 'sheep rocks'. Matches option C.

stem: The coastal landforms depend on which of the following factors: (1) the configuration of land and sea floor (2) whether the coast is advancing (emerging) seaward or retreating (submerging) landward
solution: Coastal landforms depend both on the configuration of the land and sea floor and on whether the coast is emerging (advancing) or submerging (retreating). Both factors matter. Matches option C.

stem: Which of them are not formed due to the erosional feature of the waves?
solution: Cliffs, sea caves and stacks are erosional landforms of waves. Beaches are depositional landforms formed by the accumulation of sediment. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Alluvial fans are formed when streams flowing from higher levels break into foot slope plains of low gradient. (2) The particles of the alluvial fans are light weighted, hence get deposited at the foot slope plains. (3) Alluvial fans in humid areas show normally low cones with gentle slope from head to toe and they appear as high cones with steep slope in arid and semi-arid climates. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Alluvial fans form where streams from higher levels debouch onto low-gradient foot-slope plains, so (1) is correct. The coarse, heavy load is dumped as the gradient and velocity drop suddenly — the particles are not 'light weighted' — so (2) is wrong. Fans are low, gentle cones in humid areas and high, steep cones in arid/semi-arid areas, so (3) is correct. Correct statements are (1) and (3). Matches option B.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Deltas are like alluvial fans but develop at a different location. (2) Unlike in alluvial fans, the deposits making up deltas are very well sorted with clear stratification. (3) Alluvial fans' deposits are well sorted with clear stratification. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Deltas resemble alluvial fans but form at the mouth of a river, so (1) is correct. Delta deposits are very well sorted with clear stratification, so (2) is correct. Alluvial fan deposits are NOT well sorted or clearly stratified, so (3) is wrong. Correct statements are (1) and (2). Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following: (1) The floodplains in a delta are called delta plains. (2) Natural levees are found along the banks of large rivers. (3) Meander bars are found on the concave side of meanders of large rivers and are sediments deposited in a linear fashion by flowing waters along the bank. (4) Jhelum forms meanders in its youthful stage. How many of the above are correct?
solution: Floodplains in a delta are called delta plains, so (1) is correct. Natural levees occur along the banks of large rivers, so (2) is correct. Statement (3) reproduces the NCERT description of point/meander bars verbatim, so it is treated as correct. The Jhelum, flowing over the flat floor of the Kashmir valley, is the classic example of a river forming meanders in its youthful stage, so (4) is correct. All four statements are correct. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Corrected B->D after cross-check with the official key. Note: geomorphologically point/meander bars deposit on the CONVEX (inner) bank, but statement (3) copies NCERT's wording ('concave side'), so an NCERT-keyed test marks it correct.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Meander is a type of landform. (2) As meanders grow into deep loops, the same may get cut-off due to erosion at the inflection points and are left as ox-bow lakes. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution: A meander is not a landform but only a type of channel pattern, so (1) is wrong. As meanders grow into deep loops they can be cut off at the inflection points and left behind as ox-bow lakes, so (2) is correct. Only (2) is correct. Matches option B.

stem: Many valley sinks together form:
solution: Sinkholes and dolines coalesce into valley sinks (uvalas); when many valley sinks join together they form a large, flat-floored karst depression called a polje. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Derived; 'valley sinks/uvalas' coalescing form a polje. Confirm the intended key.

stem: Which of the following is sometimes used to refer to the collapse sinks?
solution: The term doline is sometimes used to refer to collapse sinks (sinkholes formed by the collapse of a cave roof). Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following statements: (1) Lapies are formed due to the depositional process of groundwater. (2) The lapies field may eventually turn into somewhat smooth limestone pavements. Which of the above is not correct?
solution: Lapies are formed by the erosional (solution) action of groundwater, not deposition, so (1) is not correct. A lapies field may eventually be worn down into smooth limestone pavements, so (2) is correct. Only (1) is not correct. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following with reference to the karst topography: (1) Areas where limestones are dense, massive and occurring as thick beds, cave formation is prominent. (2) Caves having openings at both the ends are called tunnels. Which of the above is correct?
solution: Where limestones are dense, massive and thickly bedded, cave formation is prominent, so (1) is correct. Caves with openings at both ends are called tunnels, so (2) is correct. Both statements are correct. Matches option C.
